topic: Hip fracture analgesia and nerve block
usual_baseline: Fascia iliaca block rates are low: 2.0% [1500], 6.4% documented within 2 hours [1555], 24.5% [1394], 35% in ED [1150], 65% [1518]. Contraindications documented in 0% [1518]. Regular postoperative paracetamol 3 g/day in 16% [1462]. Pain re-evaluation within 30 minutes 52.5% [1518].
fix_that_works: Teaching the block plus an enforced proforma: FICB 24.5% to 44.3% [1394]. Education, carts, audit and feedback: 2.0% to 22.6% [1500]. Nurse audit and feedback: paracetamol 16% to 60%, no change in control [1462]. A mandatory analgesia checklist: first analgesia 130 to 38.8 minutes, FICB time 228 to 63.4 minutes, contraindications documented 0% to 64.3% [1518].
fix_that_fails: Checklist and practical sessions did not raise FICB use (65% to 65%) or pain re-evaluation (52.5% to 50%) [1518]. The 50% block target was not met (22.6%) [1500]. Preoperative paracetamol barely moved, 9% to 16% [1462].
consultant_advice: Block rate audits are common and usually end with teaching. Measure what actually limits uptake. Timestamped block recording is often missing, 43.2% in one audit [1555], so fix documentation first. Pain re-assessment after analgesia and regular paracetamol are less audited and stayed poor.
